passage: Session note, Tuesday. Karthik arrived shaking with anger. Sabina, his partner in their small design studio, had moved the two biggest clients to her own new firm without telling him. He said he wanted to post everything about her online and "make sure nobody hires her again." I asked him to hold that thought for a day and not send anything tonight. We listed what he could do instead: gather the emails and contracts in one folder, read the partnership agreement, and book a consultation with a lawyer. He stopped pacing about halfway through. Before leaving he said, "I can be furious and still not do something I'll regret." I will check in on Friday to see whether the folder exists.

qa.q: What had Sabina done to make Karthik so angry?
qa.a: Sabina had moved the two biggest clients to her own new firm without telling him.

qa.q: What was Karthik feeling and wanting at the start of the session?
qa.a: He felt furious and wanted to expose Sabina online so nobody would hire her again.

qa.q: What calm steps did the narrator suggest to protect Karthik and his work?
qa.a: Gather the emails and contracts in one folder, read the partnership agreement and book a consultation with a lawyer.

qa.q: What would change for Karthik's own studio if he had posted the attacks that night?
qa.a: His time and attention would likely go into the fight instead of the work and the clients he still has, and it could weaken his position.

grounding: Shows a business owner raging at a partner's betrayal and considering revenge, guided towards calm, documented steps.

passage:
Friday, 1 a.m.

I found out today. Ankita, my co-founder, my friend of eight years, has been moving our biggest clients to a new firm she registered in March. Siddharth, you idiot, I kept thinking, how did you not see it.

I've never been this angry. I wrote a long post naming her, with screenshots, ready to go. I wanted everyone in the industry to know. My finger was literally on the button.

Then I remembered Mr Rao's story, how he spent six years fighting an ex-partner and lost his health doing it.

So I saved the draft and closed the laptop. Instead I did three things: exported every email and invoice, changed the shared passwords, and booked a meeting with a lawyer for Monday.

I still hate what she did. I might hate her for a while. But I want my company and my life back, not a six-year war.

Going to try to sleep.

qa.q: When had Ankita registered the new firm?
qa.a: Ankita registered the new firm in March.

qa.q: What was Siddharth feeling with a finger on the button to post?
qa.a: Siddharth felt enraged and betrayed, wanting everyone in the industry to know what Ankita had done.

qa.q: What calm steps did Siddharth take instead of posting, and why do they help?
qa.a: Exporting emails and invoices, changing passwords and booking a lawyer protect the company and work through proper channels instead of revenge.

qa.q: What lesson from Mr Rao's story shaped Siddharth's choice?
qa.a: Mr Rao spent six years fighting an ex-partner and lost his health, showing how revenge can consume years.

grounding: Shows a young founder enraged by a partner's betrayal choosing documented, legal and calm steps instead of destroying her reputation.

Biju: is it? what do you actually want. revenge or your business safe?
Jomon: ...business safe
Biju: then: write down everything that happened, with dates. keep the partnership agreement. show it to a lawyer before you do anything else
Jomon: fine. but I'm still angry
Biju: be angry. just don't let her live in your head for 3 years
Jomon: meeting the lawyer tomorrow. and no reviews

qa.q: What was Jomon feeling when he planned to post reviews everywhere?
